assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling made aryl amines accessible under mild, general conditions and is now routine across pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and materials. It is an enabling method that a whole community adopted, with clear originality and very broad lasting impact; Pd cross-coupling was recognized in 2010, but C-N bond formation is a distinct, transformative extension.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general, ligand-controlled catalytic amination and drove it to broad scope; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor that required stoichiometric tin and is a priority question rather than an equal co-discoverer. A two-person prize is clean.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent confirmation, industrial scale-up and textbook status; recognition is fully mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Weight to give Kosugi's and Migita-type precursors versus the 1994-95 Buchwald and Hartwig advances is a judgement from my memory, not independently verified.
Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make some members regard it as incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1991 TEM identification of multiwalled nanotubes and the 1993 single-walled nanotubes opened a major carbon allotrope family with large impact on nanoscience, materials and electronics. As an electron microscopist I value that the structure was actually established by direct imaging and diffraction, though the Nobel-level question is the chemistry rather than the physics.
assessment.attribution: Iijima is the central figure with the 1991 observation; the 1993 single-wall reports were near-simultaneous from Iijima-Ichihashi and Bethune et al. Endo's earlier carbon-fibre work complicates priority, and Ichihashi is not in the credited names. I would propose Iijima with Bethune.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of confirmation; applications remain mostly materials-scale with limited commercial maturity, but scientific recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Priority disputes with earlier hollow carbon filament observations (Endo and others) are unresolved.
Whether the Academy sees nanotubes as chemistry or physics, after the 1996 fullerene prize, is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and related molecular sieves with controlled pore architecture and active sites, using organic structure-directing agents, enabled shape-selective catalysis, large-scale petrochemical and emissions-control applications (for example Cu-CHA). This is structure-to-function materials chemistry at its best, and my own structure work on zeolites informs how decisive 3D structure determination was for the field.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread: Davis for pore-size and structure-directing design, Zones for SSZ zeolites and the chabazite route, Corma for catalytic design and industrial transfer; Yu and Tsapatsis are strong but the three-name limit forces exclusions. The allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Decades of industrial use and independent confirmation; timing is mature, but the 2025 framework-materials prize may reduce appetite for another porous-material award.
uncertainties: Whether the field is better recognized through synthesis design or through catalysis is unresolved.
Proximity to the recent MOF/COF prize could count against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography with XFELs delivers room-temperature structures from micro- and nanocrystals and time-resolved structural snapshots with diffraction-before-destruction. It addresses the same small-crystal problem I work on by other means, and it provides real mechanistic structural chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the proof of principle and the diffraction-before-destruction concept; Fromme and Schlichting were central to biological applications and time-resolved work. Hajdu, Spence and others also contributed, so the three-person limit leaves out contributors, and the credited list does not fully capture the field.
assessment.maturity: Method is validated by many facilities, but the number of high-impact mechanistic discoveries is still growing and access is limited, so timing is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether the decisive credit lies with the concept, the sample delivery or the data analysis is uncertain.
The living status of some credited contributors is not something I can verify here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis turned photoexcited metal complexes and organic dyes into general tools for single-electron organic synthesis, with wide uptake in discovery chemistry and process settings. The impact is large and the mechanistic basis is well documented.
assessment.attribution: Credit is highly diffuse across seven names; Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz are the most plausible group from the supplied names for the 2008-2011 breakthroughs. MacMillan already has a laureate role from 2021, and a joint prize would raise the question of how to treat that, while Fukuzumi, König and Melchiorre predate or extend the concept.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and in broad use; the field is still moving, so the final shape of the central contribution may not have settled.
uncertainties: Attribution is contested and no clean three-person subset is obvious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silica (M41S, then SBA-15) introduced a new family of porous solids with tunable 2-10 nm pores through supramolecular templating. Originality and influence on catalysis, adsorption and nanostructured materials are high, and structure determination by electron microscopy and diffraction was central in establishing the ordered pore systems.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck at Mobil made the key discovery, Kuroda/Inagaki independently reported FSM-16, Stucky and Zhao extended to SBA-15 with larger pores, and Ryoo to ordered mesoporous carbon. Splitting discoverers from enablers is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of confirmation; commercial impact has been more modest than for zeolites, which weakens the case.
uncertainties: Industrial and application impact is limited relative to the scientific attention.
Which of the three or four independent routes is decisive is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified DFT electronic structure with ab initio dynamics, enabling first-principles simulation of liquids, solids and reactions. It is one of the most original and widely used computational methods. This is outside my core expertise, so I rely on field-wide judgement.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper by Car and Parrinello is unambiguous, so the two-person attribution is clean.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of use and extensions, although machine-learned potentials now partly supersede direct application; recognition would be timely but long-awaited.
uncertainties: Overlap with other candidates crediting Parrinello may make the committee reluctant to split his recognition.
The relative weight of chemistry versus physics is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR, TROSY-type methods and relaxation dispersion allowed structure and dynamics of large biomolecules in solution, including invisible excited states. The impact on structural biology and chemical dynamics is substantial and complements crystallography and EM.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore are the most plausible trio from the credited names; Wagner and Palmer made major contributions but attribution is broad and overlaps with Wüthrich's 2002 recognition.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently confirmed; the main question is whether it is distinct enough from the 2002 prize.
uncertainties: Distinctness from the 2002 NMR recognition is debatable.
Which contributions are decisive, such as isotope labelling, TROSY or relaxation methods, is unclear.
